findings: Cold review of F-1..F-6 under three lenses (GROUNDED / TOOTHED / ATOMIC), with every command evidence replayed at HEAD in the relay repo and every quote grep-verified against its snapshot. F-1: claim that the regression guard re-runs every EARLIER WP's deterministic checklist commands on each gate fire (not only the current gate's controls). Quote 're-run earlier WPs' deterministic checklist cmds' is verbatim at S-4 line 164 (the section-3 comment above the range(0;$i) loop); it grounds the 'earlier WPs' scope. Single claim, concrete falsifier (a fire recording regression-items for zero earlier controls, or code filtering the loop to the current WP). GROUNDED, TOOTHED, ATOMIC. F-2: claim that a single fire at contest.gate re-evaluates 26 earlier controls. Replayed command returns exactly 26; I further confirmed contest.gate carries exactly one advance-reveal (a single, non-retried fire), so 'single fire' is grounded, not assumed. Falsifier (a small constant <5 independent of depth) is a concrete observable. GROUNDED, TOOTHED, ATOMIC. F-3: comparative claim that per-fire regression count rises from 6 at survey.gate to 26 at contest.gate in the same run. This addresses the prior non-atomic/ungrounded flag: the command now emits BOTH counts and returned '6 26' on replay, so both comparison values live in this finding's OWN recorded evidence, nothing borrowed from F-2. Each gate has exactly one advance-reveal, so the per-fire framing holds. Falsifier (counts equal, or survey >= contest) is toothed and non-circular. It is one comparative claim, hence ATOMIC. GROUNDED, TOOTHED, ATOMIC. F-4: claim of 239 regression re-run verdicts across the sprint; replay returns 239. Single claim; falsifier (no regression-item verdicts, or a materially different count) is observable. GROUNDED, TOOTHED, ATOMIC. F-5: claim that the loop re-runs every earlier control unconditionally, not only those with a recorded pass. Quote 'this one re-runs every earlier control' is verbatim in S-4 (line 128, in the ledger_reg_item contrast against the arm hook's R6 keep-best pass-filter). 'every earlier control' entails the unconditional/no-pass-filter reading, so the claim is not smuggling beyond the quote; the pass/keep-best contrast it negates is present in the same source passage. One claim about the re-run set's scope. Falsifier (loop filters earlier controls by recorded pass/keep-best) is concrete and non-circular. GROUNDED, TOOTHED, ATOMIC. F-6: claim that regression re-runs dominate grading, 239 regression-item vs only 43 primary checklist-item verdicts. Command emits both counts and returned '43 239' on replay, so the whole comparative claim is grounded in its own evidence. Falsifier (checklist-item >= regression-item) is observable. One comparative claim, ATOMIC. No finding is non-atomic, ungrounded, or carries a circular/restatement falsifier; every recorded output matches replay and every quote matches its snapshot. APPROVE.
